title: Safe Lifting Operations
summary: Before a lift, everyone involved must know their roles, the rigging and hoisting hazards, and how the lift will be done. Plan the lift, check the crane and rigging, and keep people out of the swing path.
talking_points: Hold a lift planning meeting before any work begins so everyone involved knows the plan. Anyone involved in the lift should be licensed or certified and trained, if appropriate.
Check the lifting points, methods of attachment, sling angles, center of gravity, boom and swing angles, and crane orientation.
Inspect the crane and rigging before use for wear or damage. Make sure the outriggers are properly extended and supported, and that the soil or mats can bear the load.
Set the load swing path and keep everyone clear of it. Set up barricades and post warning signs around the lift zone. Do not stand in the swing radius or under the load.
Watch the weather (such as wind speed) and ground conditions. Do NOT operate the crane if it is unsafe. Do NOT lift more than the capacity of the crane or rigging.
Test the load. Raise it a few inches and hold, check capacity and balance, and test the brakes.
Keep the crane clear of obstructions, including overhead power lines, and keep a safe working clearance from them.
Keep the load under control with tag lines and push sticks. Follow the load, stay out of its path, and use clear hand signals or radio.
site_hazards_to_check: The load swing path and swing radius of the crane
Worn or damaged rigging and lifting gear
Outriggers not fully extended, or soil and mats too weak to carry the load
Overhead power lines and other obstructions near the crane
High wind or poor ground conditions
Workers not involved in the lift who are inside the lift zone
discussion_questions: Two workers were killed when a crane lifted a rigged concrete slab without a load test and the inappropriate rigging broke. How could that have been prevented?
Who is in our lift planning meeting, and what signals will we use?
Where is the swing path today, and who will be standing where?
